./requirements.html:</p></div></div><h2 style="color: var(--acreetion-green); margin-top: 3rem; margin-bottom: 1rem;">Hardware Compatibility</h2><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Processors (CPUs)</h3><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ Intel</span> Core 2 Duo and newer, Pentium 4+ (64-bit), Celeron, Atom (x86_64 only)</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ AMD</span> Athlon 64 and newer, Ryzen series, EPYC, Threadripper</p><p><span class="spec-badge warn-badge">✗ 32-bit</span> AcreetionOS is x86_64 only. 32-bit CPUs are not supported.</p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Graphics Cards (GPUs)</h3><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ Intel</span> Integrated graphics (HD Graphics 2000+) - Open source drivers built-in</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ AMD</span> Radeon HD 2000+ - Excellent open source support (AMDGPU/RadeonSI)</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ NVIDIA</span> GeForce 8 series+ - Proprietary drivers available via Pamac</p><p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; font-size: 0.9rem;"><strong>Note:</strong> NVIDIA users should install proprietary drivers for best performance:<br/><code style="background: var(--acreetion-code-bg); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 16px;">sudo pacman -S nvidia nvidia-utils</code></p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Wi-Fi Adapters</h3><p>Most Wi-Fi cards work out of the box. Some Broadcom and Realtek adapters may require additional drivers:</p><ul style="margin-left: 2rem; margin-top: 0.5rem;"><li><strong>Intel:</strong> Excellent support (iwlwifi)</li><li><strong>Atheros:</strong> Excellent support (ath9k/ath10k)</li><li><strong>Broadcom:</strong> May need <code style="background: var(--acreetion-code-bg); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem;">broadcom-wl</code> package</li><li><strong>Realtek:</strong> Usually works, some models need <code style="background: var(--acreetion-code-bg); padding: 0.2rem 0.5rem;">rtl88xxau-aircrack-dkms-git</code></li></ul><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Storage</h3><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ HDD</span> Traditional hard drives work fine (slower boot/load times)</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ SSD</span> SATA SSDs provide excellent performance boost</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ NVMe</span> Best performance for boot and applications</p><p><span class="spec-badge">✓ eMMC</span> Embedded storage on budget laptops/tablets supported</p><h2 style="color: var(--acreetion-green); margin-top: 3rem; margin-bottom: 1rem;">Performance Benchmarks</h2><table class="req-table" style="margin-top: 1rem;"><tr><td>Idle RAM Usage</td><td><strong>700 MB - 900 MB</strong> (Cinnamon desktop + system services)</td></tr><tr><td>Boot Time (SSD)</td><td><strong>5-8 seconds</strong> (UEFI, systemd-boot)</td></tr><tr><td>Boot Time (HDD)</td><td><strong>12-18 seconds</strong></td></tr><tr><td>ISO File Size</td><td><strong>~2.5 GB</strong> (includes Cinnamon + essential tools)</td></tr><tr><td>Install Size</td><td><strong>~8-10 GB</strong> after installation</td></tr></table><h2 style="color: var(--acreetion-green); font-size: 0.9rem;">Perfect for LibreOffice, Firefox, email, and light multitasking.</p></div><div class="req-card"><h3>💻 Software Development</h3><ul style="margin-left: 1.5rem; color: var(--acreetion-text);"><li>CPU: Quad-core 2.5GHz+</li><li>RAM: 8 GB</li><li>Storage: 120 GB SSD</li><li>GPU: Integrated (discrete for GPU compute)</li></ul><p style="margin-top: 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem;">Run VS Code, Docker, VMs, compile code smoothly.</p></div><div class="req-card"><h3>🎮 Gaming</h3><ul style="margin-left: 1.5rem; color: var(--acreetion-text);"><li>CPU: Quad-core 3GHz+ (or Ryzen 5+)</li><li>RAM: 16 GB</li><li>Storage: 250 GB+ NVMe SSD</li><li>GPU: NVIDIA GTX 1060+ or AMD RX 580+</li></ul><p style="margin-top: 1rem; font-size: 0.9rem;">Steam, Proton, native games. AcreetionOS runs on hardware from 2008+. As long as you have a 64-bit CPU and 2GB RAM, it will work. Performance will be best with 4GB+ RAM and an SSD.</p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Does AcreetionOS support ARM processors (Raspberry Pi)?</h3><p>Not yet. AcreetionOS currently only supports x86_64 architecture. ARM support is on our roadmap for future releases.</p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">How much RAM does AcreetionOS really need?</h3><p>The desktop environment uses ~700-900MB at idle. With Firefox and a few apps open, expect 2-3GB usage. We recommend 4GB minimum for a comfortable experience.</p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-text-bright); margin-top: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Can I dual boot with Windows?</h3><p>Yes! AcreetionOS installer (Calamares) detects Windows and can set up dual boot automatically. color: #222; font-weight:900; text-transform:uppercase;">TrumpOS (MLGA)</a><a href="#manual-downloads">Downloads</a><a href="#" data-modal-target="#donate-modal">Donate</a><a href="wiki.html">Wiki</a><a href="developers.html">Developers</a><a href="contact.html">Contact & Support</a><a href="git-tracker.html" class="btn btn-storm">Git Tracker</a><a href="https://gitlab.acreetionos.org" class="btn btn-storm">GitLab</a><a href="mastodon.html" class="btn btn-storm">Mastodon</a><a href="bsky.html" data-modal-target="#bsky-modal" class="btn btn-storm">Bluesky</a></nav></div></header><div class="search-strip"><div class="search-container"><form class="search-form" action="https://www.qwant.com/" method="GET" target="_blank"><input type="text" name="q" class="search-input" placeholder="Is AcreetionOS Better than Arch?" aria-label="Search the web with SearX"><button type="submit" class="search-btn">Search</button></form></div></div><div class="page-wrapper"><main id="main-content" class="content-feed"><article id="about" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>Welcome to AcreetionOS</h2></div><div class="box-body"><div class="article-content"><div class="article-logo-cluster"><img src="logo.webp" alt="AcreetionOS Cinnamon Desktop Interface: A polished, user-friendly environment running on an Arch Linux base" class="hero-logo-img" width="150" height="150" decoding="auto" loading="eager" fetchpriority="high"></div><p><strong>AcreetionOS is a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution based on Arch Linux.</strong> It features the Cinnamon desktop environment, XLibre stability, and a curated selection of tools designed for performance and repository sovereignty. It is the ideal choice for users seeking Arch Linux power without the configuration complexity.</p><h3>AcreetionOS Technical Specifications</h3><dl><dt>Base Distribution</dt><dd>Arch Linux (Rolling)</dd><dt>Desktop Environment</dt><dd>Cinnamon</dd><dt>Display Protocol</dt><dd>XLibre</dd><dt>Audio Server</dt><dd>Pipewire</dd><dt>Primary Goal</dt><dd>Accessibility & Ease of Use</dd></dl><h3>Our Team & Philosophy</h3><p>AcreetionOS is led by two Republicans who believe that software development should transcend partisan divides while remaining grounded in core values. Our team is proof that diversity of experience can drive innovation:</p><div class="team-members"><div class="team-member"><span class="team-member-name">Darren Clift</span><span class="team-member-role">Co-Lead Developer (Traditional Republican)</span></div><div class="team-member"><span class="team-member-name">Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva</span><span class="team-member-role">Co-Lead Developer (24, Trans Girl, Republican)</span></div></div><p style="margin-top: 1.5rem;">People often ask how a Trans Girl can be a Republican. To us, the answer is simple: <strong>Identity, religion, politics, and sexuality are separate things.</strong> One's personal identity or orientation does not dictate their views on governance, fiscal responsibility, or individual liberty. This separation is how it should be—allowing individuals to be their authentic selves while contributing to a shared vision for a better future through technology.</p><p><strong>We don't care about our politics when it comes to helping our community.</strong> We are here to be honest about our background, but our focus is 100% on the work. We are here to build software and make the world a better place. No more pretending; we are who we are, and we're proud of it.</p><p><strong>AcreetionOS</strong> is an approachable and user-friendly distribution based on the powerful <a href="https://archlinux.org" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Arch Linux</a> core. Our mission is to bridge the gap between the power and flexibility of Arch and the simplicity that everyday computer users expect. We aim to make the Arch ecosystem accessible to a wider audience—from students and developers to casual desktop users—by providing a stable, pre-configured, and beautiful desktop experience right out of the box.</p><p>Beyond our main distribution, Co-Lead Developer Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva has also launched <strong><a href="https://arttulos.acreetionos.org" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ArttulOS</a></strong>—a side project focused on absolute stability and a future where computing exists in the "greys," providing a seamless experience without the burden of constant choice.</p><p>This project is made possible by the incredible work of the Arch Linux developers and the broader open-source community. We see ourselves as curators, taking an already fantastic base and adding a layer of convenience, rigorous testing, and thoughtful design to create a cohesive and welcoming operating system for everyone.</p></div></div></article><article id="philosophy" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>Project Status & Community Evolution</h2></div><div class="box-body"><div class="article-content"><h3>Official Clarification: Independence & Integrity</h3><p>To ensure our community and the broader Linux ecosystem have accurate information, we are issuing the following clarification: <strong>Ben Fitzpatrick, his team, and StormOS are not part of AcreetionOS, nor have they ever been.</strong> No hostility is meant by this statement; we simply wish to be technically and organizationally transparent.</p><p>There has been a notable amount of confusion due to a video by <strong>Jack Heifier</strong> that misrepresented AcreetionOS as being part of or affiliated with Ben’s team. We want to be clear that <strong>this was not Jack's fault</strong>. Jack reported on the information he had at the time, but the misrepresentation occurred because Ben did not communicate the project's boundaries properly. This lack of communication from Ben's side has further caused AI tools like Gemini to report an affiliation that has never existed. AcreetionOS is, and will always be, its own independent entity.</p><h3>The Reality: A Two-Person Mission</h3><p>It is important for our community to understand that AcreetionOS is currently run entirely by a father-daughter duo: Darren and his daughter Natalie. We manage the development, the infrastructure, the support, and the logistics out of our own pockets. While we are passionate and dedicated, we are human, and we need your support to reach our full potential.</p><h3>The Long Road to Root</h3><p>While our <strong>Discord server will always remain open</strong>, we are beginning a very slow, multi-year migration toward <strong><a href="https://rootapp.gg/AC0V5bagggqKtuj_B_MzFA" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Root</a></strong>. This decision is driven by the restrictive policies that Discord continues to push on its users. We believe in platform freedom, and we hope that by the time this migration is complete, Root will be ready to serve as our permanent, independent home.</p><h3>How You Can Contribute</h3><p>AcreetionOS is a community-driven project, and we welcome contributions from everyone. Because there are only two of us, your help is more than just "appreciated"—it's vital. Here are the primary ways you can help us grow:</p><ul><li><strong>Developers Wanted:</strong> We would love to have more developers jump on board! Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, we accept all kinds of commits. If you want to help build the future of Linux, our doors are open.</li><li><strong>Social Media Presence:</strong> We are looking for one or more volunteers to help us manage our social media. Our goal is to have a consistent presence—ideally <strong>two posts per day, five days a week</strong>. If you can help us tell our story to the world, please get in touch.</li><li><strong>Testers & Documenters:</strong> We need eyes on our builds and hands on our guides. Help us find bugs and make our documentation the best it can be.</li><li><strong>Advocates & Sponsors:</strong> Help us spread the word or provide resources like mirrors. Every bit of outreach helps us stay independent.</li></ul></div></div></article><article id="under-the-hood" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>Under the Hood</h2></div><div class="box-body"><div class="article-content"><p>AcreetionOS is more than just a themed version of Arch Linux. We've made several key decisions and customizations to improve the user experience, stability, and performance.</p><h3 class="tech-detail-heading">Why XLibre over Wayland?</h3><blockquote style="border-left: 3px solid var(--acreetion-purple); padding-left: 1rem; margin-left: 1rem; color: var(--acreetion-text-bright);"><p><strong>Notice:</strong> We are migrating to XLibre in calendar year 2026. We are in the middle of this migration, and you can find the latest editions in our downloads section.</p></blockquote><p>AcreetionOS prioritizes the <strong>XLibre</strong> foundation (based on X11) over the current industry push for Wayland. We believe that while Wayland is promising, it still lacks the absolute reliability required for professional and production workflows. Many users still face issues with screen sharing, global keyboard shortcuts, and compatibility with specialized hardware or NVIDIA legacy drivers. By sticking with XLibre, we ensure a stable, mature environment where your software "just works" without the configuration headaches currently common in Wayland-based compositors.</p><h3 class="tech-detail-heading">Boot Process: Simple & Reliable</h3><p>We use a combination of bootloaders to ensure a smooth experience. The live environment is booted using <code>systemd-boot</code> and <code>syslinux</code> for maximum hardware compatibility. For the final installation, we use <code>grub</code>, a powerful and widely-supported bootloader. This hybrid approach ensures that AcreetionOS boots reliably on a wide range of hardware, including both modern UEFI systems and older BIOS-based machines.</p><h3 class="tech-detail-heading">Filesystem: EXT4 for Stability</h3><p>We use the <code>EXT4</code> filesystem by default. While newer filesystems exist, EXT4 is the most mature, stable, and well-tested filesystem in the Linux world. It offers excellent performance for desktop use cases and is incredibly reliable, ensuring your data is safe.</p><h3 class="tech-detail-heading">Audio: The Power of Pipewire</h3><p>AcreetionOS uses <code>Pipewire</code> as its audio server, a modern replacement for PulseAudio. Pipewire is superior in every way: it offers lower latency, better CPU utilization, and seamless support for both consumer and professional audio applications.</p></div></div></article><article id="easy-install" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>The Easy Way: AcreetionOS USB Flasher</h2></div><div class="box-body"><p>This is the <strong>recommended method for all users</strong>. Our utility makes creating a bootable USB drive simple. Just select your downloaded AcreetionOS ISO, choose your USB drive, and click 'Flash!'.</p><div style="margin-top: 1rem; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px;"><a href="https://iso.acreetionos.org:8448/Flashing_Utility/dist/AcreetionOS%20USB%20Flasher-1.0.0.AppImage" class="btn btn-flasher">Download Flasher for Linux (.AppImage)</a><a href="https://iso.acreetionos.org:8448/Flashing_Utility/dist/AcreetionOS_USB_Flasher_Setup_1.0.0.exe" class="btn btn-flasher">Download Flasher for Windows (.exe)</a></div></div></article><article id="trusted-by" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>Trusted By</h2></div><div class="box-body"><div class="article-content"><p style="text-align: center;">AcreetionOS is proud to be mirrored by the following organizations:</p><div class="mirror-logo"><a href="https://osuosl.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Oregon State University Open Source Lab</a></div><div class="mirror-logo"><a href="https://www.rwth-aachen.de/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">RWTH Aachen University</a></div><!-- Paris mirror removed - no longer reliable --><!-- <div class="mirror-logo"><a href="https://paris.acreetionos.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Paris, France Community Mirror</a></div> --><div class="mirror-logo"><!-- Conditionally added back as long as they maintain high uptime --><a href="https://acreetionos-mirror-2-ro.privacy11.xyz/iso/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Romania Community Mirror</a></div></div></div></article><article id="manual-downloads" class="content-box"><div class="box-header"><h2>Manual Downloads (ISO Files)</h2></div><div class="box-body"><p>Use these links to download an ISO file directly.</p><h3 style="color: var(--acreetion-green); ./ermin.html:</style></head><body><a href="#main-content" class="skip-link">Skip to main content</a><header class="page-header"><div class="header-content"><a href="index.html" class="logo">Acreetion<span>OS</span></a><nav class="main-nav"><a href="index.html">Home</a><a href="TrumpOS/index.html">TrumpOS</a><a href="faq.html">FAQ</a><a href="developers.html">Developers</a><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></nav></div></header><div class="container" id="main-content"><h1>Ermin: The Evolution</h1><p>In our pursuit of excellence, we have made a significant architectural decision regarding our project management and community collaboration tools. While we previously utilized the Stoat codebase, it became clear that it did not meet our rigorous quality standards.</p><div class="highlight-box"><h2>The Technical Failure of Stoat</h2><p>In our pursuit of excellence, it became clear that Stoat did not meet our rigorous standards. Technically, the platform is unoptimized: users are forced to download over 7.2 MB of data just to reach the login screen—nearly half of which is wasted on a single file for fonts and icons. This level of bloat is inexcusable for a "lightweight" app and places a significant burden on both user battery life and the project's server costs.</p><p>It is difficult to justify the Stoat team's public concerns about "money problems" and high server costs when they are paying to send this massive amount of unoptimized data to every single visitor. It is essentially leaving the water running 24/7 while complaining about the bill. If the code were simply cleaned up, their operational costs would drop significantly.</p><p>More critically, we discovered that Stoat exposed direct origin IP addresses in network traffic. For a project claiming to be privacy-focused, exposing the "home address" of its servers is a massive security failure that makes the platform vulnerable to targeted attacks.</p></div><div class="highlight-box"><h2>A Disregard for User Privacy</h2><p>Stoat is marketed as privacy-respecting, yet it forces a hidden background "location check" (GPS ping) at launch without user consent. For users with hardened privacy settings or VPNs, this causes a "welp" error in the background. When we offered to fix this by writing code for a manual region selector, the developers gave us a flat "no."</p><p>They claimed they "legally" must track GPS location for age-restricted content—a claim that falls apart under scrutiny. Compliance is traditionally handled on the server side via IP addresses; forced background GPS polling is a choice, not a legal requirement. We refuse to build on a foundation that uses "the law" as a shield to justify forced tracking and poor engineering.</p></div><div class="highlight-box"><h2>From Stoat to Ermin</h2><p>We have officially forked the <strong>Stoat</strong> codebase to create <strong>Ermin</strong>. We are stripping out the 7.2 MB of bloat, correctly hiding origin IPs, and removing all secret tracking. Ermin is being rebuilt from the ground up to ensure it is fast, transparent, and actually respects the privacy it claims to protect.</p></div><h2>Why Ermin?</h2><p>Ermin is more than just a task tracker. It is being built as a <strong>free and open source alternative to Discord and <a href="https://rootapp.gg/AC0V5bagggqKtuj_B_MzFA" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Root</a></strong>. We believe in decentralization and user freedom, and we need a tool that reflects those values without compromising on performance.</p><h2>The Fallback Strategy</h2><p>While we currently utilize various community platforms, Ermin serves as a critical fallback. In the event that Root—or any other major platform—decides to follow the path of "Discord 2.0" (introducing restrictive policies, telemetry, or walled gardens), Ermin will be ready to serve as the primary hub for the AcreetionOS community.</p><h2>Status: Under Development</h2><p>Ermin is currently in active development. We are focusing on security, stability, and a clean, efficient codebase that can scale with our community.</p><p>Stay tuned for updates as we work toward the first stable release of Ermin.</p><div style="text-align: center; margin-top: 3rem;"><a href="https://ermin-media.acreetionos.org/" class="btn btn-storm" style="display: inline-block; padding: 1rem 2.5rem; font-size: 1.2rem; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 12px; color: black; font-weight: bold;">Go to Ermin (Alpha)</a></div></div><footer class="page-footer"><p>&copy; 2026 AcreetionOS Project.
